blocks.text: Exception handling manages errors that happen while a program runs. It prevents the program from crashing and lets it respond gracefully to unexpected situations, which improves reliability and the user's experience. Python provides built-in tools to catch and handle exceptions.

blocks.title: Tidbit
blocks.text: Exception handling helps programs manage unexpected problems without stopping suddenly.

blocks.title: Example: a database insert protected by try, except and finally (Python code; each .... is one 4-space indent)
blocks.text:
import sqlite3

try:
....connection = sqlite3.connect("school.db")
....cursor = connection.cursor()
....cursor.execute("INSERT INTO students (ID, Name, Age) VALUES (?, ?, ?)", (1, "Ali", 20))
....connection.commit()             # save changes (keeps data correct)
....print("Data inserted successfully")
except sqlite3.Error as e:
....print("Error occurred:", e)
....connection.rollback()           # undo changes if an error occurs
finally:
....if connection:
........connection.close()
........print("Connection closed")

items: try-except handles errors and prevents crashes.
commit() saves the correct data, keeping the database consistent.
rollback() cancels the changes if an error occurs.

blocks.title: Class activity
blocks.text: Write a Python program that takes two numbers from the user and uses exception handling to show an error message if the input is invalid or the user tries to divide by zero.

A program may meet different kinds of exception. Python lets one try block have several except blocks, each giving the right response to one exception type. This prevents unexpected crashes, allows proper recovery and gives better control over errors.
